design_decisions.a_pass_is_a_rise_to_a_failing_reading: adopted from the design lens (finding 3): the top rung IS 0021's REAL_FIT_FAILS reading; every verdict string, the scope and the thesis say so, and the three slopes are quoted together
design_decisions.null_first_then_the_top_rung: the null control is the first fit so the label permutation is drawn at 0021's generator state and hashes to 0021's array; the top rung's three roles follow as the reproduction of 0021 (within 0.005, else NOT RUN) before any lower rung is fitted; then rungs 1, 2, 3 ascending, the model last in each.
design_decisions.one_decade: the record's only real content outside its sealed scoring set is 0021's fit block; 1/8 of it to all of it is 2.98 doublings, 0.90 decades, under 0003's two-decade scope rule, and the sealed file names the span and the rule
design_decisions.recipes_are_fixed: 0021's M4, L3 and D1 verbatim (0022's recipes_reference): 0022 measured that searching the recipes on this content moves the model by -0.0004 and the logistic by 0.0003, so a search inside each rung would cost an hour per rung and change nothing the clause reads.
design_decisions.rungs_are_nested_and_family_stratified: The unit is plaintexts (source chunks), each with every one of its encoder variants, because that is what a corpus costs (0016's convention) and because the builder curve's abscissa is manufactured fragments of a fixed plaintext supply. Rungs are nested and family-stratified: per family, one seeded permutation of its chunk ids; rung d takes the first ceil(n_f / d). Every rung therefore has the fit block's family mix (py_src carries r1 0.652, r2 0.6537, r3 0.6523, r4 0.6527 of the rows), so the curve is not a change of mixture in disguise, and a lower rung is a subset of the next, so the curve is one corpus growing rather than four draws. The rows of a rung are the fit block's rows of its chunks in 0021's fit-block order, so the top rung is 0021's block row for row (the reproduction) and M4's last-10% validation split at every rung is a random tenth of that rung.
design_decisions.the_bar: the model's slope, in real-family accuracy per doubling of plaintexts over the four rungs, >= 0.005. The bar is a design choice restated from 0016, whose 0.005 was per doubling of FAMILIES under transfer - a different abscissa and regime; it is about half the builder's in-distribution per-plaintext rate (0.010093 per doubling, sealed under reference_slopes_informational), and it is the smallest rise the instrument can call a rise: 0.005 over 2.984659 doublings is an end-to-end rise of about 0.0149, roughly 574 rows of 38452. A pass is 'rises at all at the record's rate', not 'rises like the builder curve'; the fraction of the builder rate is a flag.
design_decisions.the_bootstrap_clause: the 2.5th percentile of the model's slope under the sealed cluster bootstrap over the scored real chunks is > 0. The interval is over the scored chunks only: it does not resample the fit side (which plaintexts fell into the lower rungs, where early stopping halted), so it is expected to be narrow and this clause is expected to bind only when the slope is already near 0. A slope at or above the bar whose interval reaches 0 is REAL_CURVE_FLAT: four points and a rise the scored chunks do not agree on is not a rise.
design_decisions.the_projection_is_dropped: adopted from the design lens (finding 2): a straight-line extrapolation to 0022's bar counted plaintexts that do not exist and targeted a bar the design's own logistic curve says moves; the sealed file now states that no extrapolation beyond the top rung is banked or quoted
design_decisions.the_replicate: adopted from the design lens (finding 1d): three more fits, about a minute; the smallest rung cut again under a second seeded nesting gives a direct reading of the fit-side variance the scored-chunk bootstrap cannot see, where that variance is largest; informational, never a verdict
design_decisions.what_the_bootstrap_resamples_and_what_it: the scored real chunks (1500 of them), one resample per draw for every rung and every role, so role differences are paired; it does not resample the fit side (one seed, nested rungs), and the sealed file says so under rival_explanations_run_as_arms; a second seed would be a different preregistration.

why_this_exists: 0021 read REAL_FIT_FAILS (0.1193 against a depth-3 tree at 0.0929) and 0022 read REAL_RECIPE_FAILS (a searched model at 0.1189 against a searched logistic at 0.1182; gains from the search -0.0004 and 0.0003). Both closed the recipe excuse and both named the budget excuse as the one left open: 'a scaling curve on real plaintexts (a different preregistration)'. The record's headline is a scaling law on manufactured labels over the builder's content (0.0491 accuracy per decade, 0.014787 per doubling, over 2.9031 decades); whether real content shows any such law, and whether the boosted model buys more from each doubling than a linear rule does, is the FDM-1 question asked of real content. This run asks it with the only real content the record has: 0021's fit block, cut into nested rungs of plaintexts from 1/8 of it to all of it (2.984659 doublings). It cannot reach 0003's two-decade scope rule; it is a one-decade curve and says so.
